title: 7.1.10 Lab: Write a property
description: Mutate `b.color` on a space-bar press to practice assigning a new value to an instance property. First practice with dot-notation writes.

steps.title: Change b.color when space is pressed
steps.instructions: Inside `draw()`, detect a space-bar press with `kb.presses('space')` and assign a new color to `b.color`. The box should change color on screen when you press space.
hints: Open the moSHion docs drawer on the right and find the keyboard input section for detecting key presses.

requirements.title: Assign to b.color
requirements.description: Write `b.color = ...` inside `draw()` to change the box's color property. Help: 7.1.3 (Class and instance)

requirements.title: Detect a key press
requirements.description: Use `kb.presses(...)` (or `kb.pressing(...)`) inside `draw()` to respond to keyboard input. Help: 5.2.9 (Ground-Gated Actions)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "7.1.10 Lab: Write a property". The task they were given: A Box class is given, and b = new Box() is built in setup(); draw() paints the box in b.color. Inside draw(), detect a space-bar press with kb.presses('space') and assign a new colour to b.color, so the box changes colour on screen. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. kb.presses(key) is true only on the frame the key goes down and kb.pressing(key) on every frame it is held; ' ' and 'space' are the same key. Writing a property is the object, a dot, the property name and then =. draw() runs every frame and already paints the box with fill(b.color). Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, ternaries or if-chains, semicolons, spacing, quotes, order and helper functions of their own are all fine; only a name the starter's own code already calls or reads has to keep that name. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, so the starter's STEP comments are never the student's work. Any new colour counts: a colour name, a hex string, or a value picked from an array. Comparing with === is not assigning. Building a new Box does not change b's own property. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old beginner: short sentences and everyday words.

rubric.title: Assign to b.color
rubric.description: Somewhere in draw() (or a function it calls) a new value is assigned to b.color with = (most naturally inside the key test). Missing: b.color is never assigned, or the colour goes into a different variable. Help: 7.1.3 (Class and instance)

rubric.title: Detect a key press
rubric.description: draw() (or a function it calls) tests a key with kb.presses(...) (kb.pressing(...) also counts), so the sketch responds to the keyboard. Any key counts; the space bar is what the step asks. Missing: no key test in draw(). Help: 5.2.9 (Ground-Gated Actions)
